docs.title: Tracker Tracker
docs.text: Self-hosted dashboard for monitoring your private tracker stats over time.

docs.title: What is Tracker Tracker?
docs.text:
Tracker Tracker connects to your private tracker accounts and records your stats (upload, download, ratio, buffer, seed count, bonus points, etc.) over time. It polls tracker APIs on a schedule, stores the results, and charts everything so you see trends across days, weeks, and months.

Supports UNIT3D, Gazelle, GGn, Nebulance, MAM, and AvistaZ networks. Over 40 trackers come pre-configured.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• All your trackers in one place: upload, download, ratio, buffer, rank, bonus points across all your sites
  • Historical charts: watch your stats evolve over days, weeks, and months
  • qBittorrent and Transmission integration: per-tracker torrent details, seeding counts, cross-seed stats, and live speeds
  • Tag group visualizations: turn client tags into donut charts, bar charts, and treemaps
  • Discord notifications: alerts when your ratio drops, a tracker goes down, you hit a buffer milestone, or your rank shifts

docs.title: Common Error Messages
docs.text: Error strings in the Tracker Tracker interface, with causes and fixes.

docs.title: Understanding Tracker Health
docs.text:
The status dot next to each tracker name indicates polling status:

State Color Dot Meaning healthy Cyan Glows Ratio at least twice the tracker's required ratio, or an infinite ratio (uploads with nothing downloaded), polling normally warning Amber Glows Ratio at or above the required ratio, but below twice it no-seeds Red Glows Zero active seeds on a tracker that would otherwise be healthy or warning, so nothing is uploading. Trackers that don't report a seeding count never show it critical Red Glows Ratio below the required ratio, or the tracker has warned your account, whatever the ratio error Light gray Still, dimmed The last poll failed, but polling has not paused yet paused Red Still, dimmed Polling has been automatically suspended after 4 failed polls in a row paused-user Amber Still, dimmed You paused automated polling for this tracker offline Dark gray Still, dimmed No snapshot data exists yet (tracker was just added, or all snapshots were pruned), or the latest snapshot has no usable ratio

The required ratio is the one the tracker reports for your account, or the minimum in the built-in tracker registry when it reports none. With no requirement on record, the bands assume a requirement of 1.0, so healthy starts at 2.0, warning at 1.0, and anything lower is critical. A requirement of 0 means the tracker asks for no ratio, so every ratio counts as healthy, though no-seeds and a tracker warning still apply.

When a tracker matches more than one row, paused-user wins first, then paused, error and offline, and only then the ratio states. Among those, critical outranks no-seeds, which outranks healthy and warning. So a tracker with a 1.4 ratio against a 1.0 requirement and nothing seeding shows no-seeds, because the ratio band alone would not tell you that you need to start seeding. Against a 2.0 requirement the same tracker shows critical.

docs.title: Ratio or Stats Not Updating
docs.text: Stats only change when Tracker Tracker captures a new snapshot. If your ratio, upload, or seeding count looks stale, work through this checklist.

docs.title: Step 1. Check the poll interval
docs.text:
Go to Settings → General and check Tracker Poll Interval (15–1440 minutes).

If it's 240, stats update every 4 hours. That's normal.

Fastest update rate

15 minutes is the fastest. Stats won't update more often, even with page reloads.

docs.title: Step 2. Check if polling is running
docs.text: Look at the status dot next to the tracker name. If it's paused or error, fix that first before worrying about stale stats. See Automatic Poll Pausing below for guidance.

docs.title: Step 3. Trigger an immediate poll
docs.text:
Don't wait for the next scheduled poll.

  1. Open the tracker's detail page.
  2. Click Poll Now.
  3. The page refreshes with new stats if it works.

If Poll Now returns an error, the Poll Error Banner will show the reason.

docs.title: Step 4. Check the chart time range
docs.text:
Charts show data over your selected range. A narrow range hides changes.

  • Find the day range selector in the right sidebar on Data & Analytics.
  • Try a broader range (30 or 90 days) to see historical data.
  • If only today is selected, you'll only see today's snapshots.

docs.title: Step 5. Confirm snapshots are recording
docs.text:
If Poll Now works but charts don't move, hard-refresh first (Cmd+Shift+R on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows/Linux).

Then check the Last Polled timestamp on the tracker detail page. It should match your most recent poll.

If Last Polled updated but the chart didn't, the API returned the same values. That's normal.

docs.title: Automatic Poll Pausing
docs.text:
After 4 consecutive failed polls, the tracker automatically pauses to prevent hammering a broken tracker. When this happens:

  • The status dot switches to paused
  • The Poll Error Banner appears at the top of the tracker detail page with:
  • Red "Polling Paused" heading
  • Pause timestamp
  • Last error (e.g., Authentication failed, Host not found)
  • Resume Polling button

Verify the cause before resuming

Fix the underlying problem first. If you resume without fixing it, the tracker will fail again and re-pause immediately.

docs.title: Resuming a Paused Tracker
docs.text:
1. Open the tracker detail page.
  2. Find the Poll Error Banner at the top with the last error below "Polling Paused".
  3. Fix the problem (see specific error sections below).
  4. Click Resume Polling, then Poll Now to verify immediately.

docs.title: Tracker poll errors
docs.text: These appear in the Poll Error Banner on the tracker detail page.

docs.title: Authentication failed
docs.text:
Cause: The tracker rejected the token (HTTP 401/403 or explicit "Unauthorized"/"Forbidden").

Common reasons:

  • Token was regenerated on the tracker site.
  • Token was entered wrong (whitespace, partial copy).
  • Account API access was revoked or restricted.
  • Tracker requires an IP allowlist.

Solution

  1. Log into the tracker and find your API token (usually under "Security", "API", or "Edit Profile").
  2. Copy it carefully.
  3. In Tracker Tracker, edit the tracker settings and paste the new token.
  4. Save, then click Resume Polling, then Poll Now.

docs.title: Host not found
docs.text:
Cause: DNS resolution failed for the hostname.

Solution

  1. Test: nslookup <tracker-hostname> from your Docker host.
  2. If using VPN or custom DNS, add dns: to docker-compose.yml if needed.
  3. If the tracker moved to a new domain, update Tracker Tracker. The address comes from the built-in tracker registry, so a domain change ships as a release. If no release carries it yet, open an issue naming the tracker.

docs.title: Host unreachable
docs.text:
Cause: Hostname resolved but unreachable at the network layer. Route missing or firewall blocking.

Solution

  1. Check if the tracker loads in your browser.
  2. Verify VPN or firewall routing is up.
  3. Confirm no egress firewall on Docker host is blocking outbound.

docs.title: Connection refused
docs.text:
Cause: Host reached but connection refused. Usually wrong port or the tracker's down.

Solution

  1. Confirm the tracker loads in a browser at the address shown on its detail page.
  2. If it only loads on a different port or scheme, the registry entry is out of date: open an issue naming the tracker.

docs.title: Connection reset
docs.text:
Cause: Connection established then terminated by the host. Often SSL/TLS mismatch or invalid certificate.

Solution

  1. Use https:// if required.
  2. Self-signed certificates aren't supported.

docs.title: Request timed out
docs.text:
Cause: API doesn't respond within 15 seconds. May happen during maintenance or heavy load.

Solution

  1. Wait a few minutes and try Poll Now again.
  2. If persistent, check if a proxy is adding latency.
  3. The 15-second timeout can't be changed.

docs.title: IP temporarily banned by tracker
docs.text:
Cause: Tracker's rate-limiting blocked your IP. Poll interval too short or automated requests treated as abuse.

Solution

  1. Wait for the ban to expire, typically minutes to hours.
  2. Increase Poll Interval in Settings → General to 60 minutes (or higher for sensitive trackers).
  3. Resume polling after the ban clears.

docs.title: Proxy connection failed
docs.text:
Cause: Use Proxy is enabled and the proxy is unreachable or erroring. We don't bypass required proxies.

Solution

  1. Check Settings → Proxy and verify host, port, type, username, and password.
  2. Confirm the proxy is running and reachable.
  3. Or disable Use Proxy in tracker settings.

docs.title: Cloudflare challenge blocked the request
docs.text:
Cause: Cloudflare answered with a challenge page in place of the tracker's page, and wants a browser check first.

Solution

  1. Open the tracker in the browser you copied the cookies from and pass the check.
  2. Copy the cookies again, cf_clearance included where the tracker sets it, and paste them into the tracker's settings from that same browser, since Tracker Tracker records the User-Agent of the browser you save from.
  3. TorrentLeech has no cookies to refresh. Wait a while, and raise the poll interval if the challenge keeps coming back.
  4. If the tracker paused after repeated failures, click Resume Polling, then Poll Now.

docs.title: Tracker redirected to another site
docs.text:
Cause: The tracker answered with a redirect to a different site. Tracker Tracker does not follow it, because that would send your session cookies to another host.

Solution

  1. Open the tracker in a browser and check whether it has moved to a new address.
  2. If it has, open an issue with the new address so the tracker's entry can be updated.

docs.title: Tracker redirected too many times
docs.text:
Cause: The tracker kept redirecting between its own pages without answering with one.

Solution

  1. Open the tracker in a browser and check that its pages load.
  2. If they do, check docker compose logs tracker-tracker-app for the Poll failed for tracker line and open an issue with it.

docs.title: Tracker redirected the request
docs.text:
Cause: The tracker's API answered with a redirect instead of your stats. Tracker Tracker never follows a redirect on an API request, because it could carry your API key or session cookie to another host.

Solution

  1. Check that your API key or session cookie still works on the tracker. Some trackers answer a request without valid credentials by redirecting it to their login page; if yours were revoked or expired, paste new ones into the tracker's settings.
  2. Open the tracker in a browser and check whether it has moved to a new address. If it has, open an issue with the new address so the tracker's entry can be updated.
  3. If neither, check docker compose logs tracker-tracker-app for the Poll failed for tracker line and open an issue with it.

docs.title: Stale error banner (no pause)
docs.text:
If you see a Last Error banner without "Polling Paused", a recent poll failed but not enough to trigger a pause. It clears on the next success.

No action if the last poll succeeded

The banner shows the most recent error even if later polls recovered. If the status dot is healthy, warning, or critical, polling already recovered.

docs.title: Tracker returned an unexpected response
docs.text:
Cause: The tracker answered, but with something the adapter cannot read, such as a maintenance page, a login page in place of your profile, a changed page layout, or a reply missing a field the stats need.

Solution

  1. Open the tracker in a browser and check that the site is up and that you are still logged in.
  2. Click the bug icon (Fetch raw API response) in the tracker's header to see the response that failed.
  3. If the site looks normal, the tracker may have changed its pages or API. Check docker compose logs tracker-tracker-app for the Poll failed for tracker line and open an issue with it.

docs.title: API returned <status code>
docs.text:
Cause: API returned an unexpected status. E.g., 429 = rate limit, 500/503 = server error.

Solution

  • 429: Increase poll interval and wait.
  • 500 / 503: Tracker having issues, so wait and retry.
  • Other: Check tracker's status page or forums.

docs.title: Poll failed (generic)
docs.text:
Cause: Unexpected error not matching known patterns.

Solution

Check logs: docker compose logs tracker-tracker-app for a line with Poll failed for tracker + raw error.

docs.title: Download client errors
docs.text: These appear on individual client cards in Settings → Download Clients.

docs.title: Authentication failed (qBittorrent)
docs.text:
Cause: Wrong username or password.

Solution

  1. Confirm qBittorrent credentials in its Web UI settings.
  2. Update in Settings → Download Clients.
  3. Use Test Connection to verify.

docs.title: Session expired (qBittorrent, auto-handled)
docs.text:
Cause: Session expired (HTTP 403). We re-authenticate automatically on next request.

No action needed

Handled transparently. Persistent errors are more likely wrong credentials.

docs.title: Connection refused (qBittorrent)
docs.text:
Cause: Web UI not accessible at the configured host/port.

Solution

  1. Check host and port match qBittorrent's Web UI config.
  2. Confirm qBittorrent is running with Web UI enabled.
  3. If on a different container, confirm the port is reachable.
  4. Verify SSL toggle matches qBittorrent's scheme.

docs.title: Host not found (qBittorrent)
docs.text:
Cause: DNS resolution failed.

Solution

Use the container name (if in same Docker stack) or an IP instead of a hostname.

docs.title: Request timed out (qBittorrent)
docs.text:
Cause: qBittorrent doesn't respond within 15 seconds. May happen during heavy indexing.

Solution

Wait and retry. If persistent, check qBittorrent's CPU and memory.

docs.title: Authentication and session errors (Tracker Tracker login)
HTTP 429: Too many failed login attempts
docs.text:
Cause: Auto-lockout triggered after too many failed attempts.

Solution

Wait for the lockout to expire (time shown on login page). If you can't wait, connect to the database and clear lockedUntil in the appSettings table.

docs.title: Login succeeds but redirects back to login
docs.text:
Cause: Session cookies marked Secure but app accessed over plain HTTP. Browsers discard Secure cookies on HTTP.

Solution

If using http://, no action needed on recent versions. If serving over HTTPS via proxy, set BASE_URL=https://your-domain.com in .env.

docs.title: TOTP: Invalid code
docs.text:
Cause: Code incorrect or expired (valid 30s). Clock drift invalidates codes.

Solution

  1. Sync your device clock (NTP). Even 30-60s drift breaks codes.
  2. Wait for the next code and retry.
  3. Or use a backup code (XXXX-XXXX format, one-time use).

docs.title: TOTP: Lost authenticator / no backup codes
docs.text:
Cause: No access to authenticator app and no backup codes.

Database access required

No in-app recovery. Connect to PostgreSQL and run:

UPDATE app_settings SET totp_secret = NULL, totp_backup_codes = NULL;

Then log in and reconfigure TOTP.

docs.title: Errors when adding or editing a tracker
Tracker test failed (AvistaZ / cookie-based trackers)
docs.text:
Cause: Cookie string contains a non-ASCII character (usually … from browser truncation).

Firefox and some Chromium browsers truncate long header values in their DevTools display, replacing the end with a … (ellipsis) character. If you select and copy the displayed text instead of using "Copy Value", the truncated string gets pasted into the dialog. HTTP headers can't contain non-ASCII characters, so the connection fails.

Solution

  1. Open DevTools → Network tab → click any request.
  2. Find the Cookie header in Request Headers.
  3. Right-click the Cookie header → Copy Value (do not select the text manually).
  4. Paste the full value into the Add Tracker dialog.

How to tell if your cookies are truncated

The Add Tracker dialog shows a yellow warning if it detects a … character in the cookie string. If you see this warning, re-copy using right-click → Copy Value.

docs.title: baseUrl must use https:// or http://
docs.text:
Cause: URL uses unsupported scheme (e.g. ftp://) or missing scheme.

Solution

Prefix with https:// or http://.

docs.title: baseUrl must not target localhost or a private network address
docs.text:
Cause: URL resolves to a private IP or localhost. We block these for security.

By design

Tracker URLs must be public. Internal or self-hosted trackers can't be added.

docs.title: Tracker adapter standard
docs.text:
What a tracker adapter must do, written from what the existing adapters actually do. If you are adding a site, you probably want adding-a-tracker.md instead; most new sites need a data file and no code at all.

src/data/trackers/ says what a tracker is. src/lib/tracker-platforms/ says how it is polled. If your change is a site, it is one file in src/data/trackers/ and you never open src/lib. If your change is a new way to poll, it is one file in src/lib/tracker-platforms/adapters/, and the shared code it may call lives in src/lib/tracker-platforms/helpers/.

docs.title: 1. What an adapter is, and is not
docs.text:
An adapter turns one tracker protocol into a TrackerStats. It is not the place for facts about a site. Those live in src/data/trackers/, one file per site, as plain data: name, URL, ratio rules, user classes, content categories, logo. That folder holds 55 entries plus _template.ts and the index.ts barrel.

One adapter usually serves many sites. unit3d serves 19, gazelle 9, avistaz 5, nebulance 2. The other twelve adapters serve one site each today, but that is a fact about the world, not a licence to hardcode. If your site runs a platform that already has an adapter, you are adding a data file.

Per-site variation is configuration, not a branch. buildFetchOptions in src/lib/tracker-platforms/index.ts reads unit3dAuthStyle, gazelleAuthStyle, gazelleEnrich and nebulanceAuthParam off the registry entry and passes them in options. No family adapter contains a hostname test, and none should gain one.

docs.title: 2. The required contract
docs.text:
export interface TrackerAdapter {
  fetchStats(baseUrl, apiToken, apiPath, options?): Promise<TrackerStats>
  fetchRaw(baseUrl, apiToken, apiPath, options?): Promise<DebugApiCall[]>
}

All sixteen implement both. fetchRaw is still declared optional at src/lib/tracker-platforms/contract.ts; treat it as required.

docs.title: 2.1 The null versus zero rule
docs.text:
null means the tracker does not report this figure. 0 means the tracker reported zero. Never write a literal 0, false or true into a field because the response did not carry one.

This is the most important rule here. It has already caused shipped bugs (9f8aaa5, c83f96c). A run of fabricated zeroes cannot be told apart from an account that genuinely stopped seeding, and it corrupts every chart drawn from snapshot history.

Eight TrackerStats fields are nullable for exactly this reason (src/types/tracker-stats.ts): group, seedingCount, leechingCount, seedbonus, hitAndRuns, requiredRatio, warned, freeleechTokens. ratio is not among them; it is derived, never read (see 2.3).

Forbidden Why Write instead field: value ?? 0 Absent becomes a measured zero value ?? null warned: x?.warned ?? false Absent becomes a reassurance the user is not warned typeof x === "boolean" ? x : null parseInt(text, 10) \|\| 0 on scraped text An absent row parses as NaN, which \|\| 0 turns into zero tryParseCount(text) ?? null parseFloat(x) \|\| 0 for a ratio See 2.3 computeRatio(uploaded, downloaded) x ?? 0 in a second call Overwrites the honest null the first call set if (typeof x === "number") stats.f = x

An absent or blank class is null in group, never a placeholder such as "Unknown" or "User", so rank history and the rank-change alert read it as not reported. A JSON adapter that receives the class as text reads it through presentClass, and one that receives an id maps it through its own table, as DigitalCore and TR4KER do.

A JSON null on the wire is data, not an absent key. If the API declares invites: number | null and sends null, the tracker is stating the figure is unknown. Map it to null in TrackerStats and undefined in platformMeta. Never to 0.

Byte totals are never coalesced. Both are non-nullable bigint, so an absent or unreadable total cannot be reported as unknown and has to fail the poll. A JSON adapter gets that from requireBytes (3). A scraper throws when both totals are missing (the page is not a profile) and again when exactly one is unreadable, with the Unexpected response from <host>: prefix, the way parseRetrotoonProfile and parseFilelistProfile do. ?? 0n on a byte total is a violation and the conformance test flags it.

One shape that looks like a violation and is not. Say so in a comment so a reviewer does not "fix" it: || 0 on a value that came out of a \d+ capture. Unreachable. Delete it rather than explain it.

A secondary or enrichment call may only raise a field from null to a value, never coalesce an absent one down to a literal. Reference: gazelle.ts:205-206, guarding with typeof enriched.leechingCount === "number".

docs.title: 2.2 The rule does not stop at platformMeta
docs.text:
• A count the response omitted is undefined, and its key is omitted. Assign conditionally (filelist.ts:172-175) or coalesce with ?? undefined.
  • A boolean the response did not carry is absent, not false and not true. Capability flags gate what the UI tells a user they may do, and tracker-events.ts fires on a true-to-false transition, so a fabricated false invents a revocation and a fabricated true hides a real one. References: hawke.ts:106-117, avistaz.ts:303-318.
  • A flag parsed out of HTML must come from a positive match on both spellings, never from the absence of one word. avistaz.ts:313 guards the missing row but still derives !== "no", so a site renaming the value to "Disabled" would report a revoked right as granted.
  • platformMeta is JSON.stringifyed into the trackers row. bigint does not survive JSON, so store byte figures as number. Undefined members are dropped, which is what makes omit-when-absent work end to end.
  • Declare every optional-on-the-wire field optional in your meta interface. A required number forces the adapter to invent a zero in order to compile, which is a defect in the type, not in the adapter.

Return meta on every successful poll, built from what you read this poll. The scheduler only writes meta when the key is present, so omitting it leaves the previous poll's JSON in the database indefinitely, and a field that disappears upstream must be allowed to clear. Reference: unit3d.ts:299-302, which returns an object even when its one member is absent and says why.

If your tracker exposes nothing beyond TrackerStats, return no meta at all.

docs.title: 2.3 Derived values
docs.text:
• ratio is computeRatio(uploadedBytes, downloadedBytes). Sites render an infinity glyph, --- or Inf for a zero-download account, and parseFloat turns those into 0, the worst ratio the app can hold, which then fires the ratio-danger alert.
  • If you have a reason to prefer the tracker's reported ratio, the fallback must be computeRatio and a comment must say why. An account with nothing downloaded always takes computeRatio, whatever figure the tracker reports, since there is no quotient to report. Reference: the ratio field in Hawke's fetchStats and GGn's guard in ggn.ts.
  • bufferBytes is computeBufferBytes(uploaded, downloaded), unless the platform reports a signed buffer of its own, in which case say so (hawke.ts:129-132).

docs.title: 2.4 Errors
docs.text:
Adapter errors are sanitized by sanitizeNetworkError before a user sees them, and the sanitizer matches on wording. Wording is an interface, not prose.

  • A payload that could not be read starts with `Unexpected response from ${host}: `, naming the hostname. Documented at unit3d.ts:187-189. This is what makes the card say "Tracker returned an unexpected response" rather than "Poll failed". It applies to scrapers too.
  • Never put the word "invalid" in a message unless it really is a credential problem. The sanitizer maps /Credentials.*missing|invalid/i to "Invalid credentials", so any message containing "invalid" anywhere will send the user to re-enter a working key.
  • Do not call sanitizeNetworkError yourself. Throw the raw shape and let the caller classify.
  • Do not classify by matching digits or words in a message. Read response.status, or check the error type. helpers/errors.ts records why SessionExpiredError is a class rather than a recognisable string. Prefix any tracker-supplied string before throwing it, or a remote body containing "invalid" decides the classification for you.
  • A body that fails to parse is not a connection failure. classifyFetchError applies only to an error thrown by fetch, and classifyProxyFetchError only to a proxyFetch rejection. Every json() from adapterRequest already goes through readJson in helpers/adapter-fetch.ts, where a SyntaxError becomes the shape wording and only the remaining branch is classified. An adapter that parses text itself follows parseJsonSafe in digitalcore.ts.
  • Log through log from @/lib/logger, in the structured log.warn({ err }, "message") form, never console. The in-app event feed is built by parsing pino output, so a console.warn failure is invisible to the operator. Reference: torrentleech.ts:110.
  • A SessionExpiredError from any call aborts the poll. Every other secondary-call failure is logged and leaves its fields null.

docs.title: 2.5 Credentials
docs.text:
• Never write a credential into an Error, a log line, or a DebugApiCall endpoint, data or error. The debug route scrubs only data; the rest depends on adapter discipline. No adapter leaks today, and that is worth keeping true.
  • Parse the credential blob outside the try in fetchRaw, so a bad blob throws to the route instead of becoming a call entry. Reference: filelist.ts:287-288.
  • A JSON blob is parsed with parseCredentialJson, declaring required fields in fields and per-account ones in optionalFields. Never call JSON.parse(apiToken) yourself.
  • A pasted Cookie header goes through validateCookieHeader. It validates a whole header. An individual cookie value you interpolate yourself is outside its scope and needs your own semicolon, control-character and non-Latin-1 guard, like validateMamId (mam.ts:83).
  • A plain token sent in a request header goes through validateHeaderToken first, before the first request and outside fetchRaw's try, and the header carries the value it returns. A token placed in a query parameter or POST body relies on URLSearchParams encoding and needs no such check.
  • userAgent is required for a cookie scraper, because the session is fingerprinted against the agent it was issued to. It is optional for a JSON API, where the transport supplies one. A session the adapter logs in for itself passes none, and loginRequest and fetchTrackerHtml send the app's.

docs.title: 2.6 fetchRaw and the debug view
docs.text:
fetchRaw powers the debug dialog. It is the screen someone opens when a poll is failing, so it must not lie.

  • Return the unmodified response body in data for a JSON API. Mapping is fetchStats's job. A scraper may substitute parsed output, because the raw artifact is a whole HTML page.
  • Apply every failure test fetchStats applies. adapterFetch throws on a non-2xx, so through it the only failure reaching fetchRaw intact is one the tracker wrapped inside an HTTP 200 body (an adapterRequest caller can read a non-2xx body too, as nebulance.ts does), and the debug view marks a call healthy purely on error being null. Put every check fetchStats makes on a 200 body in one function both methods call, and in fetchRaw set error: pollError(() => thatFunction(data, hostname)), keeping the body in data. The dialog prints that body under the error. Nothing fetchStats does with that body afterwards may throw. References: creditedTotals in tr4ker.ts, readIndex in gazelle.ts. A call whose failure fetchStats tolerates takes its error from the function that decides the failure, so the entry shows the reason fetchStats logs. Reference: profileFailure in gazelle.ts.
  • Emit an entry for a call you skipped, with data: null and a reason. A debug view that simply ends after one entry cannot be told from a one-call adapter.
  • Do not abandon later calls when an earlier one fails if a cached value can satisfy the dependency. options.remoteUserId is that cached id, and a failing first call is exactly when the second call's output matters most. An id read from a body the poll rejects does not count, since the poll never makes the call that id would drive.
  • Apply the same pacing fetchStats applies. The debug route runs both methods in one request, so a missing pause means one press issues every request back to back.
  • Build the endpoint string first and derive the URL from it, so the two cannot encode differently. Reference: torrentleech.ts:377-380.
  • label is Title Case and names what the call fetches.

docs.title: 3. Shared helpers
docs.text:
Everything in src/lib/tracker-platforms/helpers/ exists because at least two adapters had already written it. Import it rather than writing it again.

Helper File Use it for Do not hand-roll adapterFetch helpers/adapter-fetch.ts Every JSON API request on the happy path. Applies the shared timeout, default User-Agent and proxy, refuses every redirect, throws on non-2xx. Your own fetch, timeout, proxy branch or non-2xx message adapterRequest helpers/adapter-fetch.ts Same, but returns a non-2xx other than a redirect instead of throwing. Only when your API reports errors in the body of a non-2xx. Reaching for this by default fetchTrackerHtml helpers/html-fetch.ts Every authenticated page fetch in a scraper. Handles headers, cookies, the redirect chain, the off-origin refusal. A private fetch with a Cookie header, your own redirect following loginRequest helpers/login-session.ts Each request of a login flow that posts the user's password, where the adapter needs the Set-Cookie and Location of the answer. Same proxy, timeout and app User-Agent as the helpers above, never follows a redirect, and classifies a failure by transport. Your own fetch or proxyFetch for a login, and the biome exception it would need withLoginSession helpers/login-session.ts The poll that runs on such a login. Caches the session per site and per whole credential set, and logs in again once on SessionExpiredError. A private session map, a key without the password, a retry keyed on the message pollError helpers/poll-error.ts fetchRaw, on every 200 body fetchStats reads. Runs the function fetchStats reads it with and returns the message that function throws, or null. Restating fetchStats's checks inside fetchRaw normalizeWhitespace helpers/html-parse.ts Any text you compare against a literal label. Labels carry U+00A0, which an exact match will not survive. value.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim() datePrefix helpers/html-parse.ts Slicing YYYY-MM-DD off a site-printed datetime Your own date regex tryParseCount helpers/html-parse.ts Any site-printed count. The first number in the text, commas stripped, decimals and sign kept, undefined when there is none. parseInt(text, 10) with your own NaN test tryParseSiteBytes helpers/html-parse.ts Site-printed byte totals. Strips grouping commas and canonicalises the unit, so both 1,024 kB and 1 GiB parse. Returns undefined rather than throwing. A private parseBytes wrapper with its own tolerances isCloudflareChallenge, isCloudflareInterstitial helpers/html-parse.ts Telling a Cloudflare challenge apart from the page you asked for. isCloudflareChallenge (the interstitial or a Turnstile widget) on an authenticated page; isCloudflareInterstitial on a login page, which can embed Turnstile of its own. fetchTrackerHtml already runs the full check on a 403 or 503. Your own html.includes("cf_chl_opt") test requireBytes helpers/bytes.ts A byte total a JSON API is contracted to send. Throws naming the host and the field when it is absent or not a number, because both byte totals are non-nullable bigint and cannot hold unknown. floatBytesToBigInt straight off the wire, which answers 0n for an absent field presentClass helpers/class-name.ts The class a JSON API sends as text for group. Returns it, or null when it is absent, blank or not a string. class ?? "Unknown", or class \|\| null, which keeps a whitespace-only class computeRatio, computeBufferBytes @/lib/data-transforms ratio and bufferBytes Reading the tracker's ratio with no computeRatio fallback parseCredentialJson helpers/cookie-credentials.ts Any credential arriving as a JSON blob JSON.parse(apiToken), shape checks, and above all the error wording validateCookieHeader @/lib/tracker-credentials/cookie-header A credential that is a pasted Cookie header Prefix stripping, control-character and non-ASCII guards validateHeaderToken @/lib/tracker-credentials/header-token A plain API token sent in a request header Your own control-character and non-Latin-1 checks SessionExpiredError helpers/errors.ts Signalling that an authenticated request came back as a login page. Callers use instanceof. Matching the message text classifyFetchError @/lib/error-utils Errors thrown by fetch, only Applying it to a JSON.parse failure classifyProxyFetchError @/lib/error-utils A proxyFetch rejection, only. Keeps its reason, worded the way every tracker transport words it Your own "via proxy" message, or classifyFetchError, which keeps only the error's name or code log @/lib/logger Every log line in the adapter layer console.warn, console.error metaFor @/types/tracker-stats Narrowing platformMeta outside the adapter that produced it meta as XPlatformMeta in a component

The interface an adapter implements is contract.ts at the module root. Adapters import it as ../contract; helpers import it the same way.

The count parser is settled. tryParseCount returns undefined, not null, because platformMeta is JSON.stringifyed into the trackers row: an undefined member is dropped, a null one is stored. A null-returning parser would write the key back on every poll and defeat omit-when-absent (2.2). TrackerStats fields coalesce with ?? null where they are assigned.

Four private number parsers remain. Each reads a different input shape, so folding them in would break them:

  • ratioBarNumber (avistaz.ts) scans ratio-bar items with a label regex.
  • parenCount (torrentleech.ts) reads the number inside parentheses.
  • trailingCount (torrentleech.ts) reads the last number in a cell; tryParseCount takes the first.
  • toNumber (unit3d.ts) reads a JSON field that may already be a number. Passing one to tryParseCount throws.

All four return null because each value goes straight into a TrackerStats field (2.1). Reach for tryParseCount unless you are in one of those four shapes.

docs.title: 4. Naming and file shape
docs.text:
Settled, not open questions. Line 1 is the file's own path comment. The class is last, exported, and declares fetchStats before fetchRaw. The fetchRaw catch fallback is byte-identical everywhere: err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Request failed". All six scrapers name their transport wrapper fetchHtml. Tests use vi.spyOn(global, "fetch") with vi.restoreAllMocks() in beforeEach, and there are no skipped or .only tests.

Rule Dominant Deviation Class name flattens the filename 14 of 16 GGnAdapter and DigitalCoreAdapter keep the site's real casing. Do not rename them; the names are public. New adapters flatten. Helpers are module-scope functions 15 of 16 gazelle.ts puts one helper on the class as a private async that never touches this, so it cannot be unit-tested directly. A prefix predicts the failure mode Mixed parse* throws, tryParse* returns undefined. Whatever it is called, "not reported" must reach TrackerStats as null. Label lookups compare exactly on normalized text filelist, retrotoon A bare .includes(label) matches any cell containing it, so "Last Access IP" satisfies a "Last Access" lookup. Normalize, then compare exactly, or anchor the regex. Ignoring the persisted _apiPath 7 adapters When the path is intrinsic to the platform, ignore _apiPath so a stale persisted value self-heals, and say so in one comment naming your intrinsic path. Date shape No convention Emit one shape and say which. The scheduler preserves a bare YYYY-MM-DD exactly as printed (trackerDateStr). Adapters still emit three shapes.

The Functions: file header. 13 of 16 adapters carry one. Either generate and verify it in CI (7.7) or drop it. A manifest that drifts is worse than none, because a contributor trusts it and writes a duplicate helper. The path comment on line 1 stays either way.

Comments. filelist.ts is the calibration reference. A comment states the constraint the current code must satisfy. It does not narrate what the code used to do; git records that. No em dashes.

docs.title: 5. Pre-submit checklist
docs.text:
Scope

  • [ ] Every fact about the site is in src/data/trackers/<slug>.ts, not in the adapter.
  • [ ] My site is not already served by unit3d, gazelle, avistaz or nebulance.
  • [ ] Per-site variation is read from options, backed by a registry flag. No hostname branch.

The contract

  • [ ] Every unreported numeric field is null. No ?? 0, || 0 or parseInt(...) || 0 on a nullable TrackerStats field.
  • [ ] group is null when the class is absent or blank, never a placeholder.
  • [ ] warned is null unless the response carried an actual boolean.
  • [ ] ratio is computeRatio(...), or the reported ratio with computeRatio as fallback and a comment saying why. No || 0 anywhere in the ratio expression.
  • [ ] I never coalesce a byte total; a missing or unreadable one throws with the Unexpected response from prefix.
  • [ ] In platformMeta, an omitted figure is undefined and its key absent. No fabricated booleans. Byte figures are number.
  • [ ] My meta interface declares every optional-on-the-wire field optional.
  • [ ] platformMeta is returned on every successful poll, not guarded on emptiness.
  • [ ] A secondary call only raises a field from null to a value.

Errors and credentials

  • [ ] Every "could not read the payload" error begins with Unexpected response from <host>:.
  • [ ] No message contains "invalid" unless it is genuinely a credential fault.
  • [ ] I do not call sanitizeNetworkError myself, and I classify on response.status or an error type, never on digits in a message.
  • [ ] classifyFetchError is applied only to a fetch rejection, and classifyProxyFetchError only to a proxyFetch rejection.
  • [ ] A tracker-supplied error string is prefixed before it is thrown.
  • [ ] I parse credentials with parseCredentialJson, and a pasted header with validateCookieHeader. I never call JSON.parse(apiToken).
  • [ ] A plain token I send in a header goes through validateHeaderToken, and a cookie value I build myself has its own control-character and non-Latin-1 guard.
  • [ ] No credential appears in any error, log line, or debug endpoint, data or error.
  • [ ] Any call I make directly carries ADAPTER_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS. Calls through adapterFetch and fetchTrackerHtml get it automatically.
  • [ ] Any call I make directly that carries a credential sets redirect: "manual" and refuses the 3xx, as adapterRequest does. A followed redirect sends a custom key header or a 307 body to whatever host the Location names.
  • [ ] I log through log from @/lib/logger. There is no console. in my file.

fetchRaw

  • [ ] Credentials are parsed outside the try.
  • [ ] For a JSON API, data is the unmodified response body.
  • [ ] Every 200-body failure test in fetchStats lives in one function both methods call, and fetchRaw sets error from it through pollError, keeping the body in data.
  • [ ] A skipped call still gets an entry with data: null and a reason.
  • [ ] endpoint is built first and the URL derived from it.
  • [ ] Any pause or backoff in fetchStats is applied here too.

Shape and tests

  • [ ] Line 1 is my file's path comment. The class is last and declares fetchStats then fetchRaw.
  • [ ] I import the shared helpers rather than re-implementing them.
  • [ ] Label lookups normalize whitespace and compare exactly, or use an anchored regex.
  • [ ] A colocated <name>.test.ts exists with one describe("XAdapter.fetchRaw") block.
  • [ ] Every field I hardcode to null has a matching expect(stats.f).toBeNull().
  • [ ] A test omits the source key entirely for any coalescing path I kept.
  • [ ] A timeout rejection is asserted to produce a message naming my tracker's host.
  • [ ] My fixture states where it came from and on what date.
  • [ ] My fixture is redacted as Sharing a Response Sample describes.
  • [ ] No em dash, no .only, no .skip.
  • [ ] pnpm tsc and pnpm test:run pass. Both block CI.
  • [ ] biome check . reports nothing new. The tree currently carries 0 errors and 12 warnings; compare against that baseline.

docs.title: 6. Known outstanding work
docs.text:
Short and current. Everything else the audit found is fixed, and most of what was here is now enforced by section 7 rather than remembered.

  1. Adapters still emit three different date shapes. The scheduler no longer corrupts a bare date, so this is now consistency rather than correctness. Pick one shape and say which.
  2. digitalcore.ts still hand-rolls its credential parser. Allowlisted in the conformance test with its reason: its messages and cookie-injection guards differ deliberately from parseCredentialJson. Reconciling the wording would let the allowlist entry go.

docs.title: 6a. Calls made without documented intent
docs.text:
Most of the rules above were recovered from comments the original authors left at the site that invented them. Where a reason was written down it was followed, and where a deviation was deliberate it was declared rather than removed: DigitalCore's hand-rolled credential parser is allowlisted in the conformance test, BTN's fixed API host is declared in the contract test's registry, AvistaZ's strictParseBytes still throws where its siblings return undefined, and MAM's ?? 0 inside a guarded sum is allowlisted.

These, by contrast, were changed on a consistency argument with no evidence either way. They are recorded here so the next person inherits the reasoning instead of re-deriving it, and so anyone who knows the original intent can say so.

Change What was inferred The tradeoff Gazelle takes the 1500ms pause in fetchRaw too That its absence was an oversight The debug route runs fetchRaw and fetchStats in one request, so one press issued four calls back to back at a site strict enough to need a pause between two of them. The cost is 1.5s of extra latency on an interactive screen, and a fast debug view may have been the point. GGn's enabled is undefined when absent, not true That defaulting in two directions from one missing object was incoherent enabled ?? true may have been deliberate optimism: better to assume an account works than to show a false disabled badge on a response that merely omitted the field. FileList and RetroToon return platformMeta even when empty That the guard was an oversight unit3d.ts documents the always-return choice and its reason; these two carried no comment. But it is a tradeoff, not a pure fix: a page that parses yet yields no meta now clears the stored values instead of keeping the last known good. DigitalCore's enrichment guards leechingCount That it should match Gazelle's identical guard Unresolved contradiction: the comment at the first call says DigitalCore reports no leeching count at all, while the enrichment reads one from the profile endpoint. One of the two is wrong and the code does not say which. peersLeecher may mean peers leeching from your seeds rather than torrents you are leeching. BTN's HnR is null when unparseable, not 0 That a present-but-unparseable count is a tracker fault Marginal. The field was already null-guarded for absence; this only changes the case where BTN sends something that is not a number.

The pattern worth remembering: where a decision was written down it was found, and where it was not, intent was inferred from consistency. Consistency is a weaker signal than it looks. If you make a call like these, leave the comment.

docs.title: 7. What can be enforced mechanically
docs.text:
This is the part that matters for a crowdsourced surface. Review attention does not scale, and four of ten drifted Functions: headers are the proof. Two precedents already exist: src/data/__tests__/tracker-registry.test.ts is a CI conformance test that reads the crowdsourced data files and fails the PR on a bad entry, and biome.json already carries an error-level noRestrictedImports with a scoped overrides block.

Ordered by value per unit of effort.

docs.title: 7.1 Let the type system carry the rule
docs.text:
Change Enforces fetchRaw? becomes fetchRaw on TrackerAdapter (types.ts:308) An adapter without a debug path stops compiling. All 13 already implement it, so this is free. platformMeta?: PlatformMeta instead of restating the ten-member union A new meta type can no longer be added to one list and missed in the other. PlatformMetaMap keyed Partial<Record<PlatformType, ...>> An unknown platform key fails to compile, where today it is silent.

Done. fetchRaw is required, the ten-member union is declared once, a compile-time assertion rejects a meta registered under a platform that does not exist, and GazelleCommunity's comment counts are optional, so no type forces a fabricated zero.

docs.title: 7.2 A shared behavioural contract test (done)
docs.text:
One file iterating VALID_PLATFORM_TYPES minus custom through getAdapter. Per adapter:

Check How Catches No credential leak Build a credential containing a unique canary. Mock fetch to reject and to return 401. Assert no label, endpoint, error or thrown message contains the canary. The rule that today depends entirely on adapter discipline. The most valuable check here. Timeout names the host Mock fetch to reject with a TimeoutError. Assert the message contains the hostname. All 13 at once. fetchRaw shape Every entry has a string label, a string endpoint, and an error that is a string or null. Structural drift in the debug contract. Title Case label /^[A-Z]/ on every label. Future repeats. Bad credentials throw Pass a malformed blob to fetchRaw, assert it rejects rather than resolving with a call list. The "parse outside the try" rule, currently unanimous and unprotected.

Done, in __tests__/adapters.contract.test.ts. It iterates VALID_PLATFORM_TYPES through getAdapter, so a new adapter inherits every rule without anyone remembering to write these cases again. Adding an adapter without adding a credential to its fixture registry fails the first case, which is deliberate: that registry is the one place a contributor declares what their adapter needs to be driven. It found two BTN divergences on its first run.

docs.title: 7.3 A source-text conformance test (done)
docs.text:
Same shape as tracker-registry.test.ts, over src/lib/tracker-platforms/:

No counts here on purpose. __tests__/conformance.test.ts computes them on every run, and a number written down goes stale the moment someone fixes something, telling the next contributor a rule is aspirational when it is already green.

Assertion Notes Line 1 equals // plus the file's own path A unanimous convention, locked in. No U+2014 Prose review cannot see an em dash reliably. Covers the test files too. No banned word Locked in at zero cost. No JSON.parse(apiToken outside helpers/ Scoped to adapters/, where parseCredentialJson is the only sanctioned route. /\?\?\s*(0\|false\|true)\b/ against a small allowlist The null versus zero rule. The allowlist is the point: adding a coalescing default means adding a line with a reason, which turns a silent choice into a reviewable one. ?? 0n is in scope: a byte total is never coalesced. Each <name>.test.ts calls .fetchRaw( Every adapter's debug path is exercised somewhere. Every logic-bearing file in helpers/ has a colocated test errors.ts is declaration-only and exempt. The Functions: header lists every function the file declares Closes 7.7 for the files that carry a header. adapters/ holds adapters and nothing else The layout rule itself.

console. is not in the list. Biome owns it (7.5), at error level across the module including the test files. Two enforcers means the weaker one gets edited when it fires.

Done, in __tests__/conformance.test.ts. Failures name the file and the matched text so the message teaches the rule. Each allowlist entry carries its reason next to it: DigitalCore's hand-rolled credential parser, MAM's category sum and TR4KER's null bonus. Adding one means writing down why, which is the whole point.

docs.title: 7.4 A null-contract test generated from the source
docs.text: For each adapter, parse the source for fields assigned a literal null in the returned TrackerStats, then assert the colocated test contains a matching expect(...).toBeNull(). Most adapters already comply, so it starts mostly green, and it makes "a contributor changes requiredRatio: null to requiredRatio: 0 and the suite stays green" impossible. Regex over both files, no AST needed.

docs.title: 7.5 Biome rules (done)
docs.text:
biome.json already uses overrides with includes, so scoping is a two-block edit.

  • suspicious/noConsole at error level, scoped to src/lib/tracker-platforms/**.
  • style/noRestrictedImports scoped to src/lib/tracker-platforms/adapters/*.ts (adapters only, not helpers/), banning a direct @/lib/tunnel import with a message pointing at adapterFetch, fetchTrackerHtml and loginRequest. No adapter is exempt: a login POST that has to read Set-Cookie through the proxy goes through loginRequest.

Done. noConsole is an error across the module, and noRestrictedImports bans a direct @/lib/tunnel import from every file in adapters/. The $schema is bumped to 2.5.10 to match the installed version.

docs.title: 7.6 Targeted helper tests
docs.text:
• Done: helpers/html-parse.test.ts now exists and drives both unit families through tryParseSiteBytes. Its absence is why the binary-unit defect stayed invisible.
  • Done: a date-shape test pins that a bare YYYY-MM-DD survives unchanged.
  • Add an assertion to helpers/html-fetch.test.ts that proxyFetch receives timeoutMs: ADAPTER_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, so the two transports cannot drift.

docs.title: 7.7 Verify the Functions: header, or drop it
docs.text:
Done, in __tests__/conformance.test.ts. It fails on any function the header omits. A file with no header is left alone, so dropping the header still complies.

It only catches omissions. A name left in the header after its function is deleted passes, so that edit is still by hand.

docs.title: 7.8 What still needs a human
docs.text: State these plainly so review attention goes where it is actually needed: whether a site is really a new platform or a fork of an existing one; whether a selector is stable or incidental to one page render; whether a fixture was captured or hand-rebuilt; and whether a comment states a present constraint or narrates history.

docs.title: Adding a Tracker to the Registry
docs.text:
Adding a new tracker to an existing platform (UNIT3D, Gazelle, GGn, Nebulance, MAM, or AvistaZ) requires one file and two lines in the barrel export. No adapter code needed.

If your tracker runs on a new platform, read Tracker API Responses first, because you'll need to write an adapter before adding the registry entry.

docs.title: Before you open a pull request
docs.text:
Branch from development and open your pull request against development, not main. main is updated from development when a release ships, so a pull request against it is built on code that is weeks behind and has to be rebased before it can merge.

If the tracker's response differs from the example for its platform, include a redacted sample as Sharing a Response Sample describes.

docs.title: Standardization Philosophy
docs.text:
Every tracker file follows the same field order and completeness rules. This makes diffs clean and reviews fast.

Every field must be present, even if empty. Use "" for empty strings, [] for empty arrays, and false for booleans. Never omit fields or use undefined. If it's there, you've decided on it.

abbreviation: "" // not: abbreviation: undefined
logo: "" // not: logo: undefined
trackerHubSlug: "" // not: trackerHubSlug: undefined
bannedGroups: [] // not: bannedGroups: undefined
warning: false // not: warning: undefined

Four exceptions:

  1. Omit the stats block entirely when you don't have real data. Don't include it with undefined values.
  2. rules.fulfillmentPeriodHours, rules.hnrBanLimit, and rules.fullRulesMarkdown are truly optional, so omit them when unknown.
  3. Platform-specific fields (gazelleAuthStyle, gazelleEnrich, unit3dAuthStyle) only belong in tracker files for their own platform. Don't add them to other trackers.
  4. bonusName is optional. Set it only when the tracker calls its bonus points something other than seedbonus.

docs.title: 1. Copy the Template
docs.text:
Copy src/data/trackers/_template.ts to a new file matching your tracker's slug (lowercase, hyphens only):

cp src/data/trackers/_template.ts src/data/trackers/mytracker.ts

Full template:

// src/data/trackers/_template.ts
//
// Copy this file to add a new tracker to the registry.
//
// 1. Duplicate this file and rename it to your tracker's slug (e.g. mytracker.ts)
// 2. Fill in all fields below. Every field must be present (use "" / [] / false
//    rather than omitting). See inline comments for guidance.
// 3. Export from src/data/trackers/index.ts (add to the barrel + ALL_TRACKERS array)
// 4. Run `pnpm test` to validate your entry
//
// Set draft: true while the entry is incomplete. Draft trackers skip strict
// validation in CI, so you can submit a PR with partial data.
//
// Allowed content categories:
//   Movies, TV, Music, Games, Apps, Sports, Books, Audiobooks, Comics,
//   Manga, Anime, XXX, Documentaries, Education, Tutorials, Fanres,
//   iOS Apps, Graphics, Audio
//
// Validator checks:
//   - slug: lowercase letters and hyphens only
//   - platform: "unit3d" | "gazelle" | "ggn" | "nebulance" | "mam" | "avistaz" | "digitalcore" | "filelist" | "btn" | "iptorrents" | "torrentleech" | "hawke" | "retrotoon" | "tr4ker" | "c411" | "animebytes" | "luminance" | "custom"
//   - apiPath must match platform default:
//       unit3d     → "/api/user"
//       gazelle    → "/ajax.php"
//       ggn        → "/api.php"
//       nebulance  → "/api.php"
//       mam        → "/jsonLoad.php"
//   - url: https only
//   - contentCategories: values must come from the allowed list above
//   - language: required
//   - rules: required (minimumRatio, seedTimeHours, loginIntervalDays as numbers)

import type { TrackerRegistryEntry } from "@/data/tracker-registry"

export const mytracker: TrackerRegistryEntry = {
  // ── Identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  slug: "mytracker", // lowercase, hyphens only (e.g. "my-tracker")
  name: "My Tracker", // display name
  abbreviation: "", // short code (e.g. "ATH", "RED"), "" if none
  url: "https://example.com", // base URL (https only)
  description: "TODO", // 1-2 sentence overview

  // ── Platform & API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  platform: "unit3d", // "unit3d" | "gazelle" | "ggn" | "nebulance" | "mam" | "avistaz" | "digitalcore" | "filelist" | "btn" | "iptorrents" | "torrentleech" | "hawke" | "retrotoon" | "tr4ker" | "c411" | "animebytes" | "luminance" | "custom"
  // Platform-specific fields (uncomment for your platform):
  //   gazelleAuthStyle: "token",   // gazelle only, "token" | "raw"
  //   gazelleEnrich: true,         // gazelle only, enables enrichment call
  //   unit3dAuthStyle: "bearer",   // unit3d only, "bearer" | "query"
  apiPath: "/api/user", // unit3d: "/api/user" | gazelle: "/ajax.php" | ggn: "/api.php" | mam: "/jsonLoad.php"

  // ── Content ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  specialty: "", // what the tracker is known for (e.g. "HD Movies", "Anime")
  contentCategories: [], // see allowed list in header
  language: "English",

  // ── Visual ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  color: "#000000", // hex accent color for the tracker's detail page
  logo: "", // "/tracker-logos/mytracker_logo.svg", file must exist in public/, "" if none
  // bonusName: "TL Points", // optional, the tracker's own name for bonus points, omit if it says seedbonus

  // ── External Links ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  trackerHubSlug: "", // slug on trackerhub.xyz, if listed, "" if none
  statusPageUrl: "", // external status page URL, "" if none
  // announceHosts: ["flacsfor.me"], // optional, domains torrents announce on as checked in your client, registrable domains only, never a URL or subdomain, omit if unchecked

  // ── Community ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  userClasses: [], // [{ name: "Power User", requirements: "Upload ≥ 100 GiB" }]
  releaseGroups: [], // [{ name: "GrpName", description: "Encodes" }] or ["GrpName"]
  bannedGroups: [], // ["GroupName"], groups explicitly banned by the tracker
  notableMembers: [], // ["handle"], notable community figures

  // ── Rules ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rules: {
    minimumRatio: 0, // 0 = no minimum
    seedTimeHours: 0, // 0 = no minimum
    loginIntervalDays: 0, // 0 = no login interval policy
    // fulfillmentPeriodHours: 72,      // optional, hours to complete H&R seeding
    // hnrBanLimit: 3,                  // optional, number of H&Rs before ban
    // fullRulesMarkdown: `...`,        // optional, detailed rules as markdown string
  },

  // ── Status ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  warning: false, // true if the tracker has a known issue or is at risk
  warningNote: "", // short description of the warning, "" if none

  // ── Flags ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  draft: true, // remove (or set false) once all required fields are filled in
  supportsTransitPapers: false, // true if the tracker supports transit papers export
  profileUrlPattern: "", // e.g. "/user.php?id={id}", required when supportsTransitPapers: true

  // ── Stats (omit this block entirely if no real data is available) ───
  // stats: {
  //   userCount: undefined,
  //   activeUsers: undefined,
  //   torrentCount: undefined,
  //   seedSize: undefined,    // e.g. "500 TiB"
  //   statsUpdatedAt: undefined, // ISO 8601 date string
  // },
}

docs.title: 2. Field Reference
docs.text: Fields are documented in template order, grouped by section.

docs.title: slug
docs.text:
Type: string

The unique identifier for this tracker. Used in filenames, URLs, and database lookups. Lowercase with hyphens only.

slug: "blutopia"
slug: "my-tracker"

docs.title: name
docs.text:
Type: string

Human-readable display name. This is what users see in the UI.

name: "Blutopia"
name: "My Tracker"

docs.title: abbreviation
docs.text:
Type: string

A short code for the tracker, used in compact UI contexts. Use "" if none.

abbreviation: "ATH" // Aither
abbreviation: "RED" // REDacted
abbreviation: "" // no abbreviation

docs.title: url
docs.text:
Type: string

The base URL including protocol. HTTPS only, no trailing slash.

url: "https://blutopia.cc"

The adapter appends apiPath to this URL to make API requests.

apiPath is always a relative path beginning with /, and this is enforced by both the registry test and scripts/validate-trackers.ts. If a tracker serves its API from a different host, that host belongs in its adapter as a module constant, not in the registry; see btn.ts. Putting an absolute URL in apiPath would persist it into every user's row with no migration path back.

docs.title: description
docs.text:
Type: string

One or two sentences about what the tracker is: content focus, community reputation, anything someone might want to know before joining.

description: "The largest general music tracker (also has some software). Has an interview to join, although the wait can be notoriously long."

docs.title: platform
docs.text:
Type: "unit3d" | "gazelle" | "ggn" | "nebulance" | "mam" | "avistaz" | "digitalcore" | "filelist" | "btn" | "iptorrents" | "torrentleech" | "hawke" | "retrotoon" | "tr4ker" | "c411" | "animebytes" | "luminance" | "custom"

Which adapter handles API requests. This tells the scheduler how to fetch stats. Pick the one that matches the tracker's software.

Platform What it means "unit3d" Runs UNIT3D "gazelle" Runs Gazelle or a fork (Orpheus, Gazelle-Music, etc.) "ggn" GazelleGames only, has its own custom API "nebulance" Uses Nebulance's API "mam" MyAnonaMouse, cookie-based auth via mam_id "avistaz" AvistaZ network, cookie auth + profile scraping "digitalcore" DigitalCore, custom JSON API, uid/pass session cookies "btn" BroadcasTheNet, JSON-RPC on a separate API host "filelist" FileList, cookie auth + profile scraping "iptorrents" IPTorrents, cookie auth + profile scraping "torrentleech" TorrentLeech, username/password login + profile scraping "hawke" HawkeUno, API key against /api/profile "retrotoon" RetroToon World, cookie auth + profile scraping "tr4ker" TR4KER, API key against /api/me "c411" C411, Bearer API key against /api/user/profile "animebytes" AnimeBytes, key and username against /api/stats/personal "luminance" Luminance, username/password login + profile scraping "custom" Placeholder, not implemented yet

docs.title: gazelleAuthStyle
docs.text:
Type: "token" | "raw", Gazelle trackers only

Controls how the API token is sent in the request.

  • "token" sends the token in an Authorization: token TOKEN header (used by REDacted, Orpheus)
  • "raw" sends the token directly in the Authorization header without a prefix

Only include this field for Gazelle trackers. If you are unsure which style a Gazelle tracker uses, check docs/kb/docs/contributing/tracker-responses-gazelle.md.

docs.title: gazelleEnrich
docs.text:
Type: boolean, Gazelle trackers only

When true, the adapter makes a second API call (action=user&id=X) after the initial action=index call to get seeding/leeching counts, warned status, joined date, avatar, ranks, and community stats. Set this to true for all Gazelle trackers, because without it seeding and leeching will show as 0.

gazelleEnrich: true

Only include this field for Gazelle trackers.

docs.title: unit3dAuthStyle
docs.text:
Type: "bearer" | "query", UNIT3D trackers only

Controls how the API token is sent in the request.

  • "bearer" sends the token in an Authorization: Bearer TOKEN header (required by UNIT3D v8+)
  • "query" sends the token as a ?api_token=TOKEN query parameter (legacy UNIT3D)

Omit this field to use the default query parameter method. Set to "bearer" if the tracker's UNIT3D instance has been updated to v8+ and returns 401 with query param auth.

unit3dAuthStyle: "bearer" // Blutopia (UNIT3D v8+)

Only include this field for UNIT3D trackers.

docs.title: apiPath
docs.text:
Type: string

The path appended to url for API requests. Must match the platform's actual endpoint.

Platform Default unit3d /api/user gazelle /ajax.php ggn /api.php nebulance /api.php avistaz /profile

Almost all trackers use the platform default. Only change it if you've verified the tracker deviates.

AvistaZ trackers scrape HTML using browser cookies. All five AvistaZ sites (AvistaZ, AnimeZ, PrivateHD, CinemaZ, ExoticaZ) use the same adapter.

docs.title: specialty
docs.text:
Type: string

A short phrase describing what the tracker specializes in. Shown in the UI and used for filtering. Use "" if none.

specialty: "HD Movies"
specialty: "Music"
specialty: ""

docs.title: contentCategories
docs.text:
Type: string[]

The categories of content hosted on the tracker. Must use values from the allowed list exactly as written (case-sensitive):

Movies, TV, Music, Games, Apps, Sports, Books, Audiobooks, Comics,
Manga, Anime, XXX, Documentaries, Education, Tutorials, Fanres,
iOS Apps, Graphics, Audio

contentCategories: ["Movies", "TV"]
contentCategories: ["Music", "Apps"]
contentCategories: []

docs.title: language
docs.text:
Type: string

Primary language of the tracker. Use "English" for English-language trackers.

docs.title: color
docs.text:
Type: string

A hex color code used to theme the tracker's detail page: chart colors, scrollbar, and stat card accents. Pick something that represents the tracker's visual identity.

color: "#00d4ff" // Aither cyan
color: "#f44336" // REDacted red
color: "#7b1fa2" // GazelleGames purple
color: "#1a4fc2" // Nebulance blue

docs.title: logo
docs.text:
Type: string

Path to the tracker's logo file in public/. Only set this if the file exists. Use "" if none. SVG preferred, PNG acceptable.

logo: "/tracker-logos/aither_logo.svg"
logo: "/tracker-logos/nebulance_logo.png"
logo: ""

docs.title: bonusName
docs.text:
Type: string

Optional. The tracker's own name for its bonus points. It replaces "Seedbonus" and the "BON" unit on the tracker's bonus card and chart. Omit it if the tracker calls them seedbonus or BON.

bonusName: "TL Points"

docs.title: trackerHubSlug
docs.text:
Type: string

The tracker's slug on trackerhub.xyz, if the tracker is listed there. Used to link to its Trackerhub profile. Use "" if not listed.

trackerHubSlug: "aither"
trackerHubSlug: ""

docs.title: statusPageUrl
docs.text:
Type: string

URL to an external status page. Use "" if none.

statusPageUrl: "https://status.aither.cc/status/aither"
statusPageUrl: ""

docs.title: announceHosts
docs.text:
Type: string[]

Optional. The domains this tracker's torrents announce on. A torrent without a tracker tag is matched by its announce domain. The site's own domain always matches, but Redacted's site is redacted.sh and its torrents announce on flacsfor.me, so without this field those torrents stay unmatched.

If you're a member, open one of the tracker's torrents in your client and look at its tracker URL (in qBittorrent, the Trackers tab). List only its domain, even when that is the site's own. If you're not a member or haven't checked, leave the field out. Don't write an empty list, because a present field says someone checked.

Write each one as its registrable domain, flacsfor.me rather than tracker.flacsfor.me. Matching ignores subdomains, so the short form covers every announce host under it. An announce URL can carry your passkey in its path, its query string or a subdomain, so never paste the URL or a subdomain copied from it. The registry test and scripts/validate-trackers.ts reject both, and an empty list too. If you push a passkey by mistake, reset it on the tracker, because it stays in the PR's history after you remove it.

announceHosts: ["flacsfor.me"]

docs.title: warning
docs.text:
Type: boolean

Set to true if there is something users should know before adding this tracker (for example, known API instability). Use false when there is no known issue.

docs.title: warningNote
docs.text:
Type: string

Short description of the warning. Use "" if warning is false.

docs.title: draft
docs.text:
Type: boolean

When true, the tracker is excluded from TRACKER_REGISTRY and skips strict validation in CI. Use this while you are filling in fields. Set to false (or remove the field) once the entry is complete.

docs.title: supportsTransitPapers
docs.text:
Type: boolean

Set to true if the tracker supports the transit papers export feature. Use false otherwise.

docs.title: profileUrlPattern
docs.text:
Type: string

The URL pattern used to construct a user's profile link. Required when supportsTransitPapers is true. Use "" if not applicable.

profileUrlPattern: "/user.php?id={id}"
profileUrlPattern: ""

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
Omit the stats block entirely when you don't have real data. Don't include it with undefined values, because the absence of the block signals that stats haven't been sourced yet.

When you have data, include only the fields you know:

stats: {
  userCount: 12000,
  torrentCount: 450000,
  seedSize: "8.2 PiB",
  statsUpdatedAt: "2025-09-01",
}

Available fields:

stats: {
  userCount?: number
  activeUsers?: number
  torrentCount?: number
  seedSize?: string       // e.g. "500 TiB"
  statsUpdatedAt?: string // ISO 8601 date string
}

docs.title: 3. User Classes
docs.text:
The userClasses array documents the tracker's rank/class system. Each entry is a TrackerUserClass:

interface TrackerUserClass {
  name: string // required, display name of the class
  requirements?: string // what it takes to reach this class
  perks?: RankPerk[] // structured perks (optional, rarely populated)
  icon?: string // path to an icon (optional)
  outsideLadder?: "above" | "below" // see below; leave unset for classes earned by stats
}

For most trackers, name and requirements are enough. Write requirements as a human-readable summary. Hit the key numeric thresholds (upload, ratio, account age, seed count) without being exhaustive.

List classes lowest to highest. The dashboard's Ranks section draws the list as a stack, one rung per class earned by stats, lit up to the member's current class. Flag everything else with outsideLadder or it is drawn as a rung nobody can reach:

  • "above" for classes granted by staff, donation or invitation (Uploader, Trustee, VIP by donation, anything bought mid-ladder). A member holding one shows a full stack under that name.
  • "below" for ratio demotions and administrative states (Leech, Banned, Validating, Parked). A member holding one shows an empty stack under that name.

Only flag a bottom class when it is a penalty. LST's "Leech" is its entry class and stays unflagged.

// From aither.ts, upload-based progression
userClasses: [
  {
    name: "Leech",
    requirements: "Ratio below 0.4 — download privileges revoked",
    outsideLadder: "below",
  },
  { name: "Phobos", requirements: "Ratio ≥ 0.4. 4 download slots" },
  {
    name: "Zeus",
    requirements:
      "Upload ≥ 2 TiB or seed size ≥ 2 TiB, ratio ≥ 0.6, age ≥ 3 months, avg seedtime ≥ 10 days. 25 download slots",
  },
  // ...
  // Staff-assigned ranks follow community ranks
  {
    name: "Uploader",
    requirements: "Staff — role model uploader. Freeleech, H&R immune",
    outsideLadder: "above",
  },
]

// From redacted.ts, simpler progression
userClasses: [
  { name: "User", requirements: "Default class on registration" },
  { name: "Member", requirements: "1 week, 10 GB up, ratio above 0.65" },
  { name: "Power User", requirements: "2 weeks, 5 uploads, 25 GB up, ratio above 0.65" },
]

// From gazellegames.ts, achievement-point based
userClasses: [
  { name: "Amateur", requirements: "Default starting class" },
  {
    name: "Gamer",
    requirements:
      "600 achievement points. Invites, requests, collections, Top 10, peerlists, mass downloader",
  },
]

If the tracker has no formal class system, leave the array empty:

userClasses: []

The perks array accepts structured perk objects for when you want machine-readable perk data:

perks: [
  { type: "freeleech", label: "Freeleech on all torrents" },
  { type: "hnr-immune", label: "H&R immunity" },
  { type: "download-slots", label: "50 download slots" },
]

Valid RankPerkType values: "download-slots", "upload", "invite", "freeleech", "double-upload", "hnr-immune", "mod-bypass", "custom".

Structured perks are not required. A plain requirements string is enough for the UI to display the information.

docs.title: 4. Release Groups
docs.text:
The releaseGroups field accepts a mixed array, and entries can be either a plain string or a ReleaseGroup object:

interface ReleaseGroup {
  name: string
  description?: string
}

releaseGroups: (string | ReleaseGroup)[]

Use the object form when you have something useful to say about what the group releases. Use a plain string when the name alone is sufficient (typically for banned groups, which belong in bannedGroups instead).

// From aither.ts, objects with descriptions
releaseGroups: [
  { name: "ATELiER", description: "Main house group — high-quality 1080p encodes and remuxes" },
  { name: "Kitsune", description: "Primary — WEB-DL" },
  {
    name: "MainFrame",
    description: "Primary — 2160p encodes, secondary 1080p encodes and remuxes",
  },
  { name: "ARTiCUN0" }, // object without description, name only
]

If the tracker has no notable internal groups, or you do not know them, use an empty array:

releaseGroups: []

The bannedGroups field is a separate string[] for groups that are explicitly banned from the tracker:

bannedGroups: ["EVO", "FGT", "YIFY", "YTS"]

docs.title: 5. Rules
docs.text:
The rules field documents the tracker's seeding and account policies. The type:

interface TrackerRules {
  minimumRatio: number // required, 0 = no minimum
  seedTimeHours: number // required, 0 = no minimum
  satisfactionMode?: "any" | "all" // how the two above combine; omit unless verified
  loginIntervalDays: number // required, days before account is disabled; 0 = no policy
  fulfillmentPeriodHours?: number // total hours allowed to complete H&R seeding
  hnrBanLimit?: number // number of active H&Rs before downloading is blocked
  fullRulesMarkdown?: string[] // the full rules as markdown lines, array-join format
}

minimumRatio, seedTimeHours, and loginIntervalDays are required even if the tracker has no policy. Use 0 to mean "not enforced."

// From nebulance.ts, ratioless tracker
rules: {
  minimumRatio: 0,      // ratioless
  seedTimeHours: 72,
  loginIntervalDays: 90,
}

// From aither.ts, full policy
rules: {
  minimumRatio: 0.4,
  seedTimeHours: 120,
  loginIntervalDays: 90,
  fulfillmentPeriodHours: 480,  // 20 days to complete H&R seeding
  hnrBanLimit: 3,               // 3 active H&Rs → downloads blocked
  fullRulesMarkdown: "...",
}

docs.title: satisfactionMode
docs.text:
satisfactionMode says how seedTimeHours and minimumRatio combine when the app decides whether a single torrent is done seeding. It is optional and deliberately opt-in.

  • "any" means either threshold clears a torrent. TorrentLeech states this outright: seed to 1:1, or seed for your user class's minimum time.
  • "all" means both must be met.
  • Omitted, the app judges on seed time alone and minimumRatio keeps its other job, the account-level figure behind the ratio-danger alert and the analytics baseline.

Set it only from the tracker's own wording, and quote that wording in a comment above the rule. Setting "any" where the tracker means "and" marks torrents satisfied that are not, which is how hit and runs are earned. Leaving it off is always safe.

A mode needs a non-zero seedTimeHours or minimumRatio to act on. The registry test suite rejects one that has neither.

// From torrentleech.ts
rules: {
  // wiki.torrentleech.org/doku.php/hnr: "There are two ways for you to give
  // back to the community" - seed to at least 1:1, OR seed for the minimum
  // time required for your user class.
  minimumRatio: 1.0,
  seedTimeHours: 240,        // 10 days, the longest class requirement
  satisfactionMode: "any",
  loginIntervalDays: 0,
}

For fullRulesMarkdown, use array-join format. It keeps diffs clean and avoids multiline template literal indentation issues:

fullRulesMarkdown: [
  "## Golden Rules",
  "**1.** Do not defy the expressed wishes of the staff.",
  "**2.** Access is a privilege, not a right.",
  "",
  "## Ratio System",
  "Required ratio starts at 0.00 and rises as you download more.",
  "",
  "## Seeding Rules",
  "- Torrents must be seeded for **72 hours** after snatching.",
].join("\n"),

docs.title: 6. Register in the Barrel File
docs.text:
Open src/data/trackers/index.ts and add in three places (alphabetized):

Export block: 

export * from "./mytracker"

Import block: 

import { mytracker } from "./mytracker"

ALL_TRACKERS array: 

export const ALL_TRACKERS: TrackerRegistryEntry[] = [
  // ...
  mytracker,
  // ...
]

The const name must match what you exported from your tracker file.

docs.title: Type check
docs.text:
pnpm tsc

This catches missing required fields or type mismatches. Fix all errors before proceeding.

docs.title: Run the test suite
docs.text:
pnpm test:run

The test suite validates tracker registry entries: required fields, valid platform types, correct apiPath values per platform, valid content category names, and plain-string bannedGroups entries.

docs.title: Check it in the UI
docs.text:
1. Start the dev server: pnpm dev
  2. Go to /trackers/new
  3. Search for your tracker by name in the Add Tracker dialog
  4. Add it with a valid API token
  5. Click Poll Now on the tracker card
  6. Confirm the tracker status changes and stats appear in the dashboard

If the tracker appears in search results and polls successfully, the registry entry is correct.

docs.title: 8. Adding a Whole New Platform
docs.text:
Everything above covers adding a tracker to a platform that already has an adapter. If the tracker runs software we don't support yet, a registry entry alone is not enough. It will show up in the picker and then fail at poll time.

A new platform touches five places. Miss any one and the tracker is either invisible or unusable:

# What Where 1 The adapter itself src/lib/tracker-platforms/adapters/<platform>.ts implementing TrackerAdapter 2 Register it adapters record in src/lib/tracker-platforms/index.ts 3 Declare the platform VALID_PLATFORM_TYPES and DEFAULT_API_PATHS in src/data/platform-types.ts 4 Credential UI a CREDENTIAL_FORMS row in src/lib/credential-forms.ts 5 Credential size cap follows the kind in that row; cookie, uid-pass and login kinds get the large cap

Steps 4 and 5 are one row. tsc refuses a platform with no CREDENTIAL_FORMS row, so the part to get right is its kind. If your platform authenticates with anything other than a single API key (session cookies, a username/password pair), a token kind gives it the "API Token" textbox, which is the wrong input, and TRACKER_TOKEN_MAX (500 characters) will reject a real cookie header at the API boundary before the adapter ever runs. A cookie, uid-pass or login kind gets the 5000-character cap in all three routes at once. The two key kinds, token and token-username, keep the 500 cap.

The pull request also needs a redacted sample of the tracker's response, which becomes your test fixture and the example on the platform's page. Sharing a Response Sample covers what to scrub and how to capture it.

docs.title: Use the shared fetch helper
docs.text:
Route requests through adapterFetch (src/lib/tracker-platforms/helpers/adapter-fetch.ts) rather than calling fetch directly. It supplies the shared timeout, honours a user's configured proxy, and normalizes errors. It supports POST with a body, so JSON-RPC style APIs work too.

adapterFetch parses the response as JSON. If your tracker has no API and you have to scrape an authenticated page instead, use fetchTrackerHtml (src/lib/tracker-platforms/helpers/html-fetch.ts). It returns the raw HTML and handles the browser headers, the proxy, the timeout, and words its errors so the scheduler's sanitizer can classify them. It takes the parts that vary per tracker as options:

  • label is the tracker name used in error messages
  • sessionExpiredMessage is thrown when the server bounces you to login
  • userAgent carries the user's copied browser UA, sent with browser navigation headers; omit it if the session came from your own login request rather than a browser, and the app's User-Agent goes out instead
